name: Mistakes to Dodge When Framing a New Addition
description: Mistakes to Dodge When Framing a New Addition

step.name: Step 1
step.text: Adding a new room to your home is exciting, but it’s easy to stumble into some common pitfalls during the framing stage. Knowing what to watch out for can save you a lot of time, money, and stress! Here are a few mistakes to dodge:

step.name: Step 2
step.text: 1. Underestimating permit and inspection lag: This is a big one! Permit applications and inspection schedules can take weeks, sometimes even months, depending on your local building department. Don’t start work assuming it’ll be a quick turnaround.

step.name: Step 3
step.text: 2. Not ordering lumber early enough: Just like permits, materials can have lead times. Don't wait until the last minute to order your framing lumber, or you might find yourself waiting for supplies.

step.name: Step 4
step.text: 3. Discovering hidden conditions after demolition: Sometimes, once you start tearing things down, you find unexpected issues with the existing structure or foundation. Factor in some wiggle room for these surprises.

step.name: Step 5
step.text: 4. Poorly planning tie-in points: Connecting your new addition to the existing house requires careful planning to ensure structural integrity and weatherproofing. Make sure these details are clear in your plans.

step.name: Step 6
step.text: 5. Skipping professional help for structural changes: If your addition involves changes to load-bearing walls, the roofline, or any major structural elements, you really need an experienced framing contractor and possibly a structural engineer. This ensures safety and compliance.

step.name: Step 7
step.text: By keeping these in mind, you can ensure your new addition's framing goes much smoother. We’re always here if you need some expert guidance!
